name: Freestanding Handstand Push-Up
description: The freestanding handstand push-up performs the full handstand press without any wall support, requiring simultaneous balance, pressing strength, and proprioceptive control. The absence of wall support forces the entire posterior and anterior shoulder girdle to continuously stabilize the handstand position while generating vertical pressing force — the gold standard of shoulder pressing in calisthenics.

execution.starting_position: Kick up to a freestanding handstand on the floor. Find balance before initiating the descent.
execution.setup_instructions: Develop a 60-second freestanding handstand hold before attempting pressing reps. Practice near a wall initially in case of loss of balance.
steps: Step 1: Establish a stable freestanding handstand.
Step 2: Slowly lower the head toward the floor while maintaining balance.
Step 3: Touch or nearly touch the top of the head to the floor.
Step 4: Press back to full arm extension, managing balance with finger pressure.
Step 5: Stabilize at the top before attempting the next rep.
common_mistakes: Attempting freestanding reps without adequate handstand balance — build the hold first
Lowering too fast — the descent must be controlled to maintain balance
safety_considerations: Practice in an open area with a mat
Learn forward and sideways bail-out techniques before attempting
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension to head lightly touching floor.
coaching_cues: Press your fingertips into the floor to steer balance
